title: Coverage and whole containers
hook: A label says 8m² per litre. Fractional need is not a whole-container order.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish continuous material need from indivisible container purchases.

misconception: A fractional material requirement can always be purchased exactly.
objective: Distinguish continuous material need from indivisible container purchases.

claims.text: A fictional coverage label states 8m² per litre. Containers hold 1L; coverage is assumed exact. Scaled model; hypothetical coverage; no application guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Area=10m², A=2L and B=1.25L. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["/","x",8]]; B=["/","x",8]; x denotes Area. At x=10, A=2, B=1.25; recall at x=13: B=1.625. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Area divided by coverage gives modeled exact volume. The whole-container order rounds that result up. This ignores surface losses and product variation, so it teaches order arithmetic rather than actual application instructions.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["/","x",8]]; B=["/","x",8]; x denotes Area. At x=10, A=2, B=1.25; recall at x=13: B=1.625. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A fictional coverage label states 8m² per litre. Containers hold 1L; coverage is assumed exact. Change only Area to 13m². What is B (Exact-need) now? Correct: 1.625L. Use B's stated rule with Area=13m²: it gives 1.625L. Area divided by coverage gives modeled exact volume. The whole-container order rounds that result up. This ignores surface losses and product variation, so it teaches order arithmetic rather than actual application instructions.

At x=10, A=2, B=1.25; recall at x=13: B=1.625. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: A fictional coverage label states 8m² per litre. Containers hold 1L; coverage is assumed exact. Change only Area to 13m². What is B (Exact-need) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Area=13m²: it gives 1.625L. Area divided by coverage gives modeled exact volume. The whole-container order rounds that result up. This ignores surface losses and product variation, so it teaches order arithmetic rather than actual application instructions.

safety.assumptions: A fictional coverage label states 8m² per litre. Containers hold 1L; coverage is assumed exact.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
